question: A 42-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a 10-month history of joint pain and stiffness in her wrists and fingers. The symptoms are worse in the morning and improve with activity. Physical examination shows swelling and warmth over the MCP and wrist joints in both hands. An x-ray of the hands is shown. Synovial biopsy from an affected joint would most likely show which of the following?
analysis: The clinical presentation of joint pain and stiffness, particularly in the wrists and fingers, along with morning stiffness that improves with activity, is suggestive of rheumatoid arthritis (RA). In RA, a synovial biopsy typically shows a proliferation of granulation tissue, which is indicative of the inflammatory process associated with the disease. Other options such as monosodium urate crystals and calcium pyrophosphate crystals are associated with gout and pseudogout, respectively, while noncaseating granulomas are seen in conditions like sarcoidosis. Therefore, the most likely finding in a synovial biopsy from an affected joint in this case is proliferation of granulation tissue.
